markdown_report:
The selected experiment adds a causal recent-summary gate to the corrected NextItNet residual blocks. It targets stale-history persistence and broadly relevant recommendations that miss current purpose, while testing whether selective history use improves Electronics’ weak lower-tail separation. These are hypotheses, not measured improvements.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Recent coherent behavior sometimes identifies specific preferences. Older isolated interactions can therefore be useful candidates for suppression, without assuming recency always wins. (2) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin. Improving confusing cases deserves priority, although training margins cannot establish validation HR@10. (3) Embedding-collapse scores of 0.5071–0.5234 imply mean cosine similarities near zero. Global embedding dispersion is consequently a weaker initial target than contextual discrimination.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet expands receptive fields through causal dilated residual convolutions. This makes residual updates a natural location for selective history control [1]. (2) DyS4Rec explicitly addresses irrelevant historical interactions. It motivates filtering, but does not establish this particular gate or benchmark gains [2]. (3) R²NS motivates warm-up before informative-negative mining. Sampling offers a separate way to address confusing comparisons, with false-negative risk [3].

**Framework.** Organize interventions along three directions: history selection → residual gates; item identity → jointly learned title/description features; ranking discrimination → curriculum negatives. All preserve one jointly trained NextItNet per category. The gap addressed here is adapting receptive-field contributions to current context without requiring unavailable compatibility labels or pretrained representations.

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; difficulty increases with implementation cost. Each assessment gives a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Assessments |
|---|---|
| Recent-summary residual gate [1,2] | O 5: +contextual combination, −standard gating; P 7: +adaptive context, −may saturate; U 8: +targets stale and broad matches, −cannot verify practical fit; M 7: +targets contextual confusion, −no demonstrated margin gain; D 3: +small block change, −causal masking needs care |
| Curriculum multi-negative loss [3] | O 3: +task-focused application, −established approach; P 7: +stronger comparisons, −false negatives; U 5: +specific ranking, −indirect intent modeling; M 8: +direct separation target, −sampled-margin overfitting; D 4: +backbone unchanged, −sampling overhead |
| Joint scratch text residual | O 4: +identity-aware integration, −standard fusion; P 6: +purpose-bearing tokens, −sparse supervision; U 7: +specific item identity, −missing specifications; M 6: +distinguishes confusing items, −text can blur IDs; D 6: +single network, −token pipeline |

**Selected implementation.** For each residual block, compute a masked causal mean over the latest five hidden states. A small sigmoid projection of the current state and summary gates the dilated-convolution update. Initialize gates near one to approximate the supplied baseline; preserve its loss and optimizer for an interpretable first comparison.

Keep all four routes, seeds 0/42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Read the final nonpadding position. Save matching architecture and predictor code; preserve diagnostic interfaces. Select using pinned macro validation HR@10, with diagnostic margins as supporting evidence only.

idea.description: Add a jointly trained recent-summary sigmoid gate to each corrected NextItNet residual update, retaining one model and checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The gate explicitly targets two observed user failures: older isolated interactions persisting as current interests, and broad relevance outranking specific recent-purpose matches. It also targets contextual positive-negative confusion, particularly Electronics’ measured 12.27% sampled wrong-rank rate. It cannot establish replacement needs, accessory compatibility, or user intent from unavailable evidence.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep the supplied causal dilated convolutions, item embeddings, scoring head, training objective and optimizer initially. Compute each summary from only nonpadding hidden states at positions at or before the current position. Reapply the padding mask after each block. Initialize gate projection weights to zero and bias to 3, giving sigmoid gates near 0.95. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView, DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt. Use the actual trained network for probes. Leave unavailable metadata breakdowns explicitly unavailable. Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory. The predictor writer must embed the same gated architecture and load exactly one selected checkpoint per category. No execution or validation result is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, initialize one corrected NextItNet with seed 42.
For each causal residual block:
    mask = sequence != 0
    summary[t] = sum(h[j] * mask[j] for j in max(0,t-4)..t) / max(1, sum(mask[j]))
    update = baseline_causal_dilated_residual_branch(h)
    gate = sigmoid(Linear(concat(h, summary)))
    h = (h + gate * update) * mask[..., None]
Train using the unchanged baseline objective and sampler.
For inference:
    features = log2feats(left_padded_sequence)
    last = maximum position whose item is nonzero
    scores = predict_score(features[last], candidate_items)
    handle empty histories through the supplied baseline convention
Select the single checkpoint per category using the fixed validation protocol.
Generate working/predict.py with the identical architecture and category routing.

originality.positive: Combines causal recent-context summaries with selective residual updates inside the required NextItNet family.
originality.negative: Gating and local context summaries are established techniques; novelty is their constrained application.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small, testable mechanism for adapting effective history use and supports later analysis of gate behavior.
future_potential.negative: Gates may saturate or suppress useful long-range preferences; benchmark benefit remains unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small jointly trained projection per block and no additional dataset or independently trained component.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal masked pooling, padding behavior, checkpoint loading and embedded predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses causal dilated residual convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and residual-update locations for the proposed gate.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed recent-summary gating mechanism or its performance on this benchmark.

related_work.title: DyS4Rec
contributions: Addresses irrelevant historical interactions obscuring next-interaction intent, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: Supports selective history use conceptually; it does not verify a gated NextItNet implementation or gains here.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Combines uniform-sampling warm-up with informative-negative retrieval and curriculum reranking, according to the supplied search summary.
limitations: Hard negatives can include relevant unobserved items.
Its sampling approach is an alternative experiment, not part of the selected initial gating change.
